lead.headline: The INDIA bloc rallies at Ramlila Maidan to demand the removal of election chief Gyanesh Kumar, a day after a mock impeachment
lead.byline: THE HINDU · THE NEW YORK TIMES · 1 NOV
lead.short: Opposition leaders including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee marched to Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On Saturday the INDIA bloc held a symbolic 'public impeachment', adopting six charges against him by a show of hands, including deleting 13.2 crore voters through the revision of voter rolls.

why.text: It is the opposition's biggest show of strength against the Election Commission, and the voter-roll revision it is fighting reaches every constituency.

more: The motion was moved by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at his residence on Rajaji Marg, in a setting copied from the Lok Sabha. The charges accuse Kumar of conspiring with the BJP to steal elections and of acting at the behest of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Rahul Gandhi said Kumar should be removed and tried for treason, and that the opposition had been forced into a public impeachment because every other institution was closed to it.

The BJP's J.P. Nadda called the rally a "foolish and designed drama" and accused Gandhi of holding it on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. The Congress's K.C. Venugopal called it a "stern warning" to Modi and Shah. The Supreme Court has asked the Election Commission for a report on alleged misuse of Form 7 deletion requests in Uttar Pradesh.

seconds.headline: Youth protests over living costs turn violent in Germany and France, with shops looted in Frankfurt and 565 arrests in France
seconds.short: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday after youth-led protests over the cost of living, spending cuts and military service, with violence also in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. In France about 320,000 people marched in a third weekend of protests; police arrested 565 people, and an officer in Paris was hit by a molotov cocktail.

why.text: Europe's two biggest economies now face the young on the streets over money and conscription, and that will weigh on their budgets and defence plans.

more: The German marches were organised by the group Gen Z regelt, "Gen Z takes charge". Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin counted up to 18,000 protesters, about half the organisers' estimate. Police used water cannon against people throwing fireworks, stones and bottles. Hesse's interior minister, Roman Poseck, said about 100 identified left-wing extremists had infiltrated the Frankfurt march, and called the way it ended "shameful".

In France the turnout was down from about 410,000 the previous weekend, the interior ministry said, with 70,000 marching in Paris. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez called the attack on the officer an "attempted murder". Masked rioters prised up paving stones to throw at police at Porte de Charenton, and four police officers and a gendarme were hurt in the capital.

seconds.headline: The FBI blames North Korea for the $6.3bn Binance hack, as the exchange says it has replaced 90% of the stolen funds
seconds.short: The FBI said on Saturday that TraderTraitor, a group backed by North Korea, carried out the record $6.3bn hack of Binance on or about 29 October. Binance says it has bought back 90% of the stolen amount with its own money and began restoring withdrawals in phases on Sunday. Co-chief executive Richard Teng said users would not bear the loss.

why.text: It is the biggest theft in crypto's history, and whether Binance can cover all of it decides whether its users lose money.

more: TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, accused in 2014 of hacking Sony Pictures over The Interview, a film that mocked Kim Jong-un. The FBI said it had seen the hackers converting stolen assets into Ethereum and expected them to be laundered further through decentralised finance and instant swap services. It urged companies to block transactions linked to their addresses.

Teng said the breach was a "complex attack" that used a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity. Binance has set aside about $6.34bn of company money, part of it from its $1bn Secure Asset Fund. The remaining 10% of the tokens are less liquid and may take longer to buy, the exchange said.

facts.withdrawals: resuming in phases from Sun 1 Nov

update.new: The FBI names North Korea; Binance says 90% is covered.
update.front: The theft now has a state behind it, and the exchange says users' losses are almost covered.

seconds.headline: Apple will put Alibaba's Qwen models into Siri and Apple Intelligence in China, with testing from 4 November
seconds.short: Apple said on Saturday that Alibaba's Qwen AI models will power Apple Intelligence in China, bringing its long-delayed AI features to Chinese iPhone users. Testing starts on 4 November in the iOS developer beta, and a wider rollout follows in December with iOS 27.3. Users will reach Qwen through Siri, Apple's writing tools and its camera-based visual intelligence.

why.text: Apple has sold iPhones in China for more than two years without the AI features it launched elsewhere, and this deal is how it catches up.

more: For some requests Siri will call on Qwen's broader knowledge to answer directly, and users can ask questions about photos and documents, including PDFs and presentations. A "Compose with Qwen" option will generate text and images from a prompt, and an "Ask Qwen" button in visual intelligence will identify objects and places. Users will be asked for permission before anything is sent to Qwen.

"We are delighted to partner with Apple," said Alibaba chief executive Eddie Wu. Alibaba said requests and answers will not be used to train its models. China's cyberspace regulator registered Apple's on-device generative AI service in July, clearing the main regulatory hurdle, and Alibaba said then that Qwen would come to iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS in China.

seconds.headline: Alcaraz will face Alex de Minaur in the Vienna final after de Minaur knocks out the top seed, Zverev
seconds.short: Carlos Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev 6-4, 7-6 in the Vienna semi-finals on Saturday and plays Alex de Minaur in the final today. De Minaur, the fifth seed, beat top seed Alexander Zverev 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 on his third match point, his first win over the German outside team events in nine meetings.

why.text: Alcaraz goes for another title before Turin, against a man who has just moved into the last qualifying place for the ATP Finals.

more: The win lifts de Minaur to 3,210 points in the Race to Turin, one ahead of Rafael Jodar, for ninth place, the last ticket now that Jannik Sinner is out for the rest of the season. The Paris Masters, which starts on Monday, will decide whether he keeps it. Zverev becomes world No. 1 on Monday.

Serving at 5-6 in the final set, Zverev was two points from defeat when he lost his temper with the umpire over a time violation. He held, but lost the tiebreak after two failed serve-and-volley attempts. De Minaur, 27 and ranked 10th, is unbeaten indoors this season at 10-0 and reaches his 23rd tour final. The final starts at 18:30 IST.

update.new: Alcaraz is in the Vienna final, against de Minaur.
update.front: Alcaraz plays for a title tonight, and the shock semi-final reshapes the race for Turin.

stories.headline: Delhi bans outdoor construction and older out-of-state vehicles from today, and orders offices to keep 50% of staff at home
stories.short: Delhi's winter pollution rules took effect on Sunday. Dust-raising demolition and outdoor construction are banned, as are vehicles registered outside Delhi that fall below BS-VI emission standards, with a few exemptions. Government and private offices must keep 50% of their staff working from home, and parking charges at authorised sites are doubled.

why.text: Delhi's air turns hazardous every November, and these rules decide how millions of people get to work for the next three months.

more: The measures run from 1 November to 31 January, except the doubled parking charges, which stay until 28 February. They come from a gazette notification the Delhi government issued on 23 June. The vehicle ban covers all non-Delhi vehicles below BS-VI, not only commercial ones, and vehicles without a valid pollution certificate will not get fuel at any pump through the year.

Enforcement may be relaxed until Deepavali, The Hindu reports. Delhi's air quality index rose from 179, in the moderate band, on 20 October to 244, poor, the next afternoon, bringing the first stage of the Graded Response Action Plan into force across Delhi-NCR.

stories.headline: Thousands rally in Tel Aviv for Eisenkot to oust Netanyahu with Arab parties' support, after Tuesday's deadlocked election
stories.short: Thousands rallied in Tel Aviv on Saturday urging opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to strike a deal with Arab parties to remove Benjamin Netanyahu. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats and Eisenkot's 48 in the 120-seat Knesset, and the three Arab-led parties won 19. Counter-protesters shouted that Israel should not have a government with "terrorists".

why.text: Who governs Israel shapes the wars with Iran and in Gaza, and the Arab parties now hold the balance.

more: Eisenkot has ruled out a coalition with the Arab parties, but together they would have a comfortable majority of 67. Nearly 840,000 people voted for Ra'am and the Joint List, a 64% rise on 2022, according to the Central Election Committee. Protesters told AFP this may be the "last chance for real change" and called Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, a "great manipulator".

Netanyahu has accused the Arab parties of "stealing" the election with money from Qatar, which Qatar calls a disinformation campaign. Arab parties have offered Eisenkot support from outside government, Israeli media report. For many Israelis, siding with Arab parties remains politically unpalatable, and right-wing figures have described the high Arab turnout as "electoral terrorism".

update.new: Protesters press Eisenkot to deal with the Arab parties.

briefs.headline: GST collections rise 23% to ₹2.31 lakh crore in October, the fastest growth in more than four years
briefs.text: Gross collections reached over ₹2.31 lakh crore, up 23% on the year and the fastest growth in more than four years, with import revenue up 42%. Net collections after refunds rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore.

briefs.headline: The Centre scraps its ₹2.5 a litre export duty on petrol and raises the levy on diesel exports to ₹11.5
briefs.text: Diesel's levy rises from ₹8.5 to ₹11.5 a litre and jet fuel's from ₹10.5 to ₹11, from 31 October, while the ₹2.5 petrol duty goes. The levies came in on 27 March to keep fuel at home during the West Asia war and are reviewed every fortnight.

notes.Nifty 50: Up 0.5% at 23,053 on Friday, and 2% up on the week.
notes.Nifty IT: Up 2.3% on Friday, its highest close in three months, before the US tech rout.
notes.USD/INR: The rupee is at about 94.95 a dollar, ending October with its best month since February.
notes.Nasdaq-100: Fell 3.5% on Friday, its lowest close since July; the S&P 500 fell 1.8%.

briefs.text: Nicolas Jackson had scored his eighth goal of the season for Villa, and John McGinn missed a penalty. The home crowd sang for manager Unai Emery throughout, after the row with Jamie Carragher.

briefs.headline: Jamie Carragher apologises to Aston Villa for 'clumsy and wrong' language after the club threatened to sue him
briefs.text: He said on Saturday that his remarks about Unai Emery and Manchester United were meant to be "tongue in cheek". Villa had said on Friday they would take legal action over "unacceptable insults".

briefs.text: He has started four of Real's 13 games and played only stoppage time in the Clásico, with Denzel Dumfries also ahead of him since joining from Inter. His contract runs until 2031.

briefs.headline: Canelo Alvarez, 36, wins back the WBC super-middleweight title on a unanimous decision against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh
briefs.text: The 36-year-old won 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110, his 64th win in 69 fights, and handed Mbilli his first defeat in 31. The fight went ahead two days after missiles were intercepted over Riyadh.

briefs.headline: Kane misses a penalty as Dortmund equalise in the 89th minute to draw 2-2 at Bayern
briefs.text: Fabio Silva's goal in the 89th minute leaves both sides on 18 points, with Bayern top on goal difference. Kane hit the crossbar from the spot and later the post, one of four times Bayern struck the woodwork.

briefs.headline: South Africa beat Australia in the Cape Town decider to win the Test series, as Rabada becomes the fastest to 350 Test wickets
briefs.text: Chasing 288, Australia were 60 for seven at lunch after Kagiso Rabada, the fastest bowler to 350 Test wickets, took two in the first over. Pat Cummins blamed his batters, and David Warner called the collapse "un-Australian".

stories.headline: Hamilton takes his first Ferrari pole in Mexico, and Lawson is thrown out of qualifying for a battery breach
stories.short: Lewis Hamilton put his Ferrari on pole for the Mexico City Grand Prix on Saturday, ahead of George Russell and Charles Leclerc. Liam Lawson, ninth for Racing Bulls, was disqualified because his MGU-K power fell from 350kW to zero in an instant after his fastest Q2 lap. The race starts at 01:30 IST on Monday.

why.text: Kimi Antonelli has another chance to wrap up the drivers' title, with his Mercedes team-mate Russell starting on the front row.

more: The rules say electrical power must be cut gradually, by no more than 50 or 100kW a second. Lawson ran out of battery at the end of the lap and did not lift off the throttle straight after the line, the stewards found, so the step-down was too steep. Racing Bulls had got both cars into Q3 and were the best of the rest, in eighth and ninth.

Lawson now faces a recovery drive. Max Verstappen, who clashed with him in practice, starts with a one-place grid penalty and says he has cleared the air with him. Antonelli admitted to driving "tense" and "tired" on the cusp of the title. In Austin a week ago he needed other results to go his way, and Russell and Hamilton each finished one place higher than he needed.

update.new: Qualifying: Hamilton on pole; Lawson disqualified.

data.max_note: Third in Austin, his sixth podium in a row, and unhappy with Red Bull's tyre choices.
